conviction_note: The findings sum to a small positive (+0.9). Q3 polysilicon transaction prices rose about 34% off the late-July low and policy cut supply, against thin spot volumes and an inventory build. The scaled number is 0 (p_up 50 x abs 11) because the last three prints were all sold (-6.9%, -11.9%, -14.6%) and the bar is disputed ($77m-$140m revenue, -$0.21 to -$0.48 EPS). The gap between the two measurements is that reaction function, not an inconsistency.
bar: Disputed, so every size is capped small. Q3 2026 revenue consensus is $139.5m with EPS -$0.21 (Zacks, 1 estimate, via CNHI after the Q2 print: https://www.cnhinews.com/news/article_f9d8e36c-e7dd-54cf-9eb2-72380e6de503.html), $77.4m with non-GAAP EPS -$0.43 (Benzinga: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DQ/earnings-forecasts) and EPS -$0.48 (TipRanks). The Q2 bar was also disputed after the fact: finviz cited $114.7m revenue and -$0.53 EPS, Earnings Whispers $59.2m and -$0.28. There is no company revenue guide, only production guidance: Q3 40,000-45,000 MT and FY2026 160,000-180,000 MT (Q2 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001477641/000110465926099218/tm2623691d1_ex99-1.htm). print_vs_bar is my inference: roughly 25-30k MT sold at about $4.7-5.0/kg, i.e. $120-145m, against a bar midpoint of about $108m.
positioning_check: Short interest was 4,399,192 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 6.5% of the 67.67m ADS outstanding, with 6.56 days to cover. The peak was 5.05m on 2026-09-15, and short interest has roughly doubled from 2.1m in Oct 2025 (https://equibles.com/stocks/dq/shortinterest, read 2026-10-26). That is moderately crowded on days to cover, not extreme. In the sealed baseline, skew_25d is -6.19 vol points (upside paid) and the put/call OI ratio is 4.79. The event-implied move is 12.2%, but the ATM spread is 75% of mid, so that figure is indicative only. Spot is $10.11: -7.25% over 20 days, 0.3% above the 52-week low, 71.7% below the 52-week high. Goldman's Sell rating carries a $10 target (stockanalysis.com).

findings.finding: China n-type rod polysilicon transaction prices (Silicon Industry Branch) rose from RMB 32,000/t in the week of 22 Jul to RMB 43,000/t in the week of 17-23 Sep (+34%), and held at 43,000 through the 21 Oct weekly print. So Q3 realised ASP should sit clearly above Q2's $4.04/kg (cash cost $4.57, total cost $5.95). Inventory marked to NRV at Q2-end prices (Q2 impairment $55.7m) is now being sold above its carrying value, which points to a smaller impairment and a narrower gross loss than Q2's $82.7m. Q4 opens at the higher price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DQ has not paid for revenue or margin lines lately. Q4'25 (26 Feb 2026) beat on EPS and still fell 6.85% intraday on a revenue miss (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1145858192). Q1'26 (29 Apr) fell 11.85% (sealed tape; the volume spike confirms the event day). Q2'26 (20 Aug) fell 14.6% on an EPS miss despite a sequential revenue rise (https://finviz.com/news/383985/daqo-new-energy-shares-tumble-after-q2-earnings-miss-and-weak-polysilicon-market).
findings.why_not_priced: The industry price is public. Yet DQ fell 7.25% over 20 days to within 0.3% of its 52-week low while the price it sells at rose about a third, so the tape is not carrying the ASP improvement. The consensus EPS range of -$0.21 to -$0.48 is far narrower than Q2's -$1.20 and may partly carry it. If it were fully priced, the stock would have recovered off the post-Q2 lows rather than making new ones.
findings.independence: The 21 Oct weekly report confirms prices flat at 43,000 (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026102100037768). On the Q2 call (20 Aug) management cited transactions near RMB 40/kg and said spot was beginning to recover (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262122110-tradingkey). Both are proxies; there is no company Q3 ASP.

findings.finding: Q3 sales volume is the swing line, and the evidence points both ways; net slightly positive. On 20 Aug management said shipments 'continued to pick up in the third quarter', that 'selling and shipping our product is really not an issue', and that it targets about 15% market share and lower inventory. Q2 sales were only 15,190 MT against 43,675 MT produced, and H1 was 87.1k produced against 19.7k sold. Against that, the industry's weekly reports show thin spot trade: the 28 Sep release was the first official price in almost two months, only 2-4 firms were transacting, and new orders were slow as of 21 Oct. A revenue bar of $77-140m implies roughly 16-29k MT at about $4.8/kg, so modest volume growth clears the low end. If Q3 sales stay well below the 40-45k MT production, the inventory and cash-burn worry continues.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume drove the last two prints. In Q1'26, sales of 4,482 MT against 38,167 MT in Q4'25 coincided with -11.85%. In Q2'26 volume recovered to 15,190 MT but ASP fell, and the stock dropped 14.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: No Q3 volume figure has been published. Xinjiang Daqo (688303) releases its Q3 report on 2026-10-28 per its disclosure calendar (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/688303/event.html), so the number arrives with DQ's own release. Consensus revenue spans almost 2x ($77m-$140m), which is what an unresolved volume line looks like.
findings.independence: The counter-evidence on thin spot trade comes from different sources: https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260928/c680289466.shtml and https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026102100037768. H1 production and sales come from Pacific Securities' interim note (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H3_AP202609221829741877_1.pdf, 2026-09-22, snippet only).

findings.finding: Industry production cuts began in October: the Silicon Industry Branch expects utilization of about 35% from October, and a 30 Sep weekly projected October output of about 105k t, down 12.9% month on month. DQ's Q4 production guide is therefore likely to come in at the low end of, or below, what the FY guide implies (FY 160-180k MT less H1 87.1k and Q3 40-45k leaves about 28-53k MT for Q4). That supports price, but at about 57% of nameplate capacity already, a lower utilisation raises unit cost and idle-capacity charges, and the market has sold DQ's lower-volume quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Feb 2026 the FY26 production guide (140-170k MT) came with a revenue miss and the stock fell about 6.9%. No print in the history isolates a production-guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry-level cuts are public; DQ's own Q4 number is not. Its 9 Oct IR record said only that it will set its pace by market supply and demand (https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1643057.shtml). The sign of the market's reading of a cut, price support or unit-cost drag, is not observable in advance.
findings.independence: The 9 Oct Xinjiang Daqo IR record calls 'actual output changes' the core industry variable (https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1643057.shtml). The October output projection comes from https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026093000036747 (2026-09-30, snippet only).

findings.finding: Positioning leans toward a squeeze on any non-negative print. Short interest is 4.4m shares (about 6.5% of ADS), days to cover 6.56 at the 30 Sep settlement, roughly double a year ago. The stock is 0.3% above its 52-week low and at Goldman's $10 Sell target, and the option skew pays for upside (-6.19 vol points).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints all fell (-6.9%, -11.9%, -14.6%) with short interest lower than now. No squeeze has shown up on a print in this history.
findings.why_not_priced: Skew and price already show it: upside is paid and the stock is at its lows. This is a modest positive on how a near-bar print could trade, not an unpriced fact.
findings.independence: Skew comes from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options); the Goldman $10 Sell target from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/dq/. Different data from the same theme.

findings.finding: Market cap is about $686m (67.67m ADS x $10.11) against $1.92bn of cash, short-term investments, bank notes, HTM and fixed deposits and zero debt at 30 Jun (Q2 6-K), part of it attributable to Xinjiang Daqo's minority holders. The Q2 release disclosed no active ADS repurchase program, only $7.8m of buybacks at the subsidiary. A new ADS buyback or a capital-return statement on the call would land on a stock trading well below its cash.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No capital-return announcement in the reaction history I could establish.
findings.why_not_priced: The discount to cash is long-known and priced as cash trapped in China and pledged to AIDC diversification. Only an announcement inside the window would change it, and I found no source saying one is coming, so this is sized as an option, not an expectation.
findings.independence: The 9 Oct IR coverage cites about RMB 10.4bn of cash and a 7.9% debt ratio at Xinjiang Daqo (https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1643057.shtml).

findings.finding: Cash is being steered into diversification. In June Xinjiang Daqo committed about RMB 6bn to a Kunshan AIDC energy-systems manufacturing base. Per the 9 Oct IR coverage the project is still at the early permitting stage and the R&D is early, so any capex or progress update on the call is a use of the cash a value holder wants returned.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The A-share hit limit-up on the 4 Jun 2026 announcement (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/688303/event.html). There is no print-day reaction to this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the announcement is four months old. Only a capex number or a funding change on the call would be new.
findings.independence: Q2 call coverage (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/DQ) notes the AIDC power-equipment entry via affiliate Daqo Group.

findings.finding: Downstream demand is weak: China's Jan-Jul 2026 new PV installations were 86.15 GW, -61% year on year, and chain-wide inventory was estimated at about 500k t in early September. That caps how far the price recovery passes through to Q4 volumes and to the outlook management gives.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 20 Aug management deferred the market's improvement to 2027, and the stock fell 14.6% that day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is a public macro series, and the stock at its lows reflects it. It is filed as a proxy for the outlook commentary.
findings.independence: Proxy, snippet only. The 21 Oct weekly cites a downstream price inversion blocking pass-through (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026102100037768).

searched_and_found_nothing: A Q3 volume or ASP figure from Daqo or Xinjiang Daqo before the print: none. The 688303 Q3 report is scheduled for 2026-10-28, and the 9 Oct IR record gives no numbers.
A Q3 2026 print from a peer polysilicon producer (Tongwei, Wacker, GCL) before 27 Oct: none found.
A dated sell-side Q3 preview for DQ from late October: none found.
An active DQ ADS buyback authorisation in 2026: none in the Q2 release or the search results.
The polysilicon consolidation (收储) platform's October execution: nothing concrete found.
Short interest for the 15 Oct settlement: not yet published (FINRA due 26 Oct).

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive and agree with the upside-paid skew. They cut against the -7% 20-day run-up and against DQ's own reaction function: three straight prints sold for 6-15%. So p_up is held at 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar): the bar has three sources that disagree, so every finding stays capped under 1 point. Finding 1 went from +1.0 to +0.7.
Rule 1 (fact vs reaction): the last three prints were sold. p_up moved from 52 to 50 and expected_move_pct from +0.44 to 0. Finding 1 was already cut under rule 6 and is not cut again.
Rule 5 (proxy): the installations macro series went from -0.5 to -0.3.

Rule 3 (contradictions): the Q3 volume evidence was already merged into one finding before the file was read; Q3 volume moved from +0.5 to +0.4 after rereading its own caveat (production still far above sales).
Rule 7: short interest was already checked; the sign agrees with the skew, so nothing changed.
